section_summary: This section concludes W. Henry Lawrence Jr.’s memorandum on a September 1948 visit to Hokkaido. It examines labor disputes, communist influence, industrial production, education, policing, population, and prospects for a peace treaty, followed by the memorandum’s itinerary, contact list, and supporting documents. The section then begins a separate London despatch reporting British parliamentary debate on Japan’s economic recovery and its implications for British trade.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on conditions in Hokkaido following an official visit
subfiles.from: W. Henry Lawrence Jr., Foreign Service officer, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports on political, economic, labor, educational, and Occupation conditions observed during Lawrence’s September 1948 visit to Hokkaido.
subfiles.summary: The surviving conclusion assesses communist influence in labor unions, railway and communications disputes, coal and industrial production, wage demands, and the shortage of heating fuel. It discusses police capacity, repatriates, industrial development, finance, unsettled reparations, possible sabotage, the purge, and decentralization. Later sections examine Hokkaido University and school governance, democratic education, Occupation personnel, and Japanese hopes for an early peace treaty with continuing protection. The memorandum closes with a list of sixteen enclosures and a distribution note.

subfiles.title: Itinerary of Foreign Service Officer W. H. Lawrence Jr. on visit to Hokkaido
subfiles.about: Lists Lawrence’s rail, ferry, and automobile travel from September 17 to 28, 1948.
subfiles.summary: Records stops and travel times between Tokyo, Hokkaido towns, and the return route.

subfiles.title: Japanese officials and business people met during the Hokkaido trip
subfiles.about: Names the officials, managers, labor representatives, bankers, educators, and students Lawrence met in Hokkaido.
subfiles.summary: The list identifies interviewees by organization and position across government, industry, labor, banking, and Hokkaido University.

subfiles.title: Notification concerning student political movements
subfiles.to: Prefectural governors and presidents and heads of higher institutions
subfiles.about: Sets out the Education Ministry’s position on student political activity and school neutrality.
subfiles.summary: The notification permits political study and discussion while opposing party branches, outside control of schools, disruption, and student movements modeled on labor disputes. It also addresses political responsibility, tuition payments, and rumored university regulations.

subfiles.title: Arrests of national railway employees in connection with labor disputes
subfiles.about: Tabulates railway workers’ desertion from work, warrants, arrests, detention, prosecution, and release by district.
subfiles.summary: Two OCR renderings of the same table give a grand total of 1,056 deserters and 399 arrests.

subfiles.title: Arrests of all communications workers in connection with labor disputes
subfiles.about: Tabulates warrants and arrests involving communications workers at Hokkaido offices.
subfiles.summary: Lists postal and communications offices by prosecutorial district and gives district totals.

subfiles.title: Cases handled by public procurators in the Sapporo High Public Procurators Office jurisdiction
subfiles.about: Summarizes criminal cases received, disposed of, and pending from January through August 1948.
subfiles.summary: Records 60,899 cases received across Sapporo, Hakodate, Asahikawa, and Kushiro districts.

subfiles.title: Fixed number of procurators and administrative officers
subfiles.about: Compares authorized and present procuratorial staffing by office.
subfiles.summary: Shows 298 personnel in post against 358 authorized positions, a shortage of 60.

subfiles.title: Japanese text of notification concerning student political movements
subfiles.to: Prefectural governors and heads of higher institutions
subfiles.about: Provides the Japanese original of the translated notification on student political activity.
subfiles.summary: The original accompanies the English translation and addresses students’ political participation, school neutrality, and educational guidance.

subfiles.title: Japanese originals of procuratorial statistics
subfiles.about: Provides Japanese source tables corresponding to the translated staffing, case, and labor arrest statistics.
subfiles.summary: A cover page precedes Japanese tables of procuratorial staffing and case dispositions, followed by labor arrest figures.

subfiles.title: Unions Told to Kick Out Communist Leadership
subfiles.from: Rutherford Poats, United Press correspondent, in the Nippon Times
subfiles.about: Reports Richard L. G. Deverall’s call for Japanese unions to reject communist leadership and form a labor party.
subfiles.summary: Deverall criticizes communist union tactics and urges independent political organization by labor unions.

subfiles.title: The Far East in Parliament
subfiles.about: Transmits excerpts from British parliamentary debate on Japan and Far Eastern economic policy.
subfiles.summary: The despatch quotes Mr. Rhodes on the Occupation, Japanese trade unions, zaibatsu influence, population growth, and the potential impact of Japanese textile production on British mills. It then quotes William Teeling on trade among Japan, China, and Hong Kong and on Britain’s position in a Japanese peace settlement. The discussion continues beyond page 480.
